title: 3.7.16 Plain English to Pseudocode: Spread vs. Rest, Side by Side
description: Turn four plain-English steps into pseudocode for the body of total(...numbers): the same gathering loop whether the caller spreads an array or lists the numbers.

steps.title: Turn the plain-English steps into pseudocode
steps.instructions:
Here is the plan in plain English:

**1.** Start the running total, `sum`, at 0.

**2.** Go through the numbers one at a time.

**3.** For each number, add it to `sum`.

**4.** When there are no more numbers, give back `sum`.

The same plan is drawn as a flow chart above the editor (open the Flow Chart bar). You do not draw it, you read it: the loop is the hexagon and the diamond, and `FOR EACH` does both jobs, so the diamond has no line of its own.

In `README.md`, type these as numbered pseudocode **between the first and last line**. Your four steps take **five** lines, because END FOR is a line too. Number every line, including the indented line and the END FOR line (not the last line of the editor). Indent the line inside the loop. The loop is always `FOR EACH` here, even where earlier JavaScript used an index. Call the running total `sum` or `total`. Each keyword looks like this, in a different program:

- `SET lives TO 3` (start a value)
- `FOR EACH enemy IN enemies` ... `END FOR` (the loop)
- `SET score TO score + 10` (a step inside the loop that adds)
- `RETURN lives` or `OUTPUT lives` (the answer, after the loop)

Plain English is fine here. Press **Grade** above the editor: the AI reads what your steps mean and marks each Quest card green or red. Changing your text clears its marks, so press Grade again when you have finished editing.

Before you submit, trace `total(5, 5)` and then `total(...scores)` with `scores` holding `[5, 5]`. The same steps give 10 both times: the rest parameter gathers the arguments into `numbers`, and the spread spreads them out to be gathered.
hints: The loop is `FOR EACH ... END FOR`, and the steps inside it are indented.
Whatever happens once the loop is over comes after END FOR, not inside it.

requirements.title: Numbered steps
requirements.description: Number your steps 1. 2. 3. and so on, with something written after each number.
requirements.hint: Write at least four lines that start with a number, each with a step written after it.

requirements.title: The total starts at zero, before the loop
requirements.description: The running total starts at zero, before the loop begins.
requirements.hint: Start the sum at zero once, before the FOR EACH. Do not start it again inside the loop.

requirements.title: One loop over numbers, closed
requirements.description: One loop over numbers, closed with an END line such as END FOR.
requirements.hint: Loop over numbers once with FOR EACH, and close it with END FOR. Start each of those on its own line.

requirements.title: Each number is added to the total, inside the loop
requirements.description: Each pass adds the loop's number to the running total.
requirements.hint: Inside the loop, add the number to your running total.

requirements.title: The total is given back after the loop
requirements.description: The total is handed back once the loop is over.
requirements.hint: After the loop is closed, give back the total.

requirements.title: Nothing is given back inside the loop
requirements.description: The answer comes after END FOR, not between FOR EACH and END FOR.
requirements.hint: Either there is no FOR EACH loop yet, or a step inside it returns. That would end the method after the first number. Give the answer back once, after the loop ends.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your steps
aiCheck.prompt: The student was given four plain-English steps and rewrote them as numbered, step-by-step pseudocode in README.md, between a first line and a last line that were already there. The program they were describing is the body of total(...numbers): start a running total called sum (or total) at 0; go through the numbers one at a time; for each number, add it to the total; when there are no more numbers, give back the total. Judge each criterion ONLY by whether its idea is present in the student's steps, however they word it. Plain English, keywords such as SET, FOR EACH, END FOR, RETURN, OUTPUT, or a mix of both are all fine, and so are different names, different capitalisation, and different ways to number the lines. Do not require any particular keyword. A step that is clearly aimed at the criterion is enough for 'met'. Mark a criterion 'missing' only when the idea is absent or the steps do the opposite, for example giving back the total inside the repeating part for the last criterion. Write each note for THIS student's own steps: in a not-met note, name the exact step or word in their steps that causes the problem (quote at most a few words), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected steps. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their steps satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.

rubric.title: Numbered steps
rubric.description: The student numbered their steps (1. 2. 3. or similar), at least four of them.

rubric.title: The total starts at zero, before the loop
rubric.description: A running total (sum, total, or the student's own name for it) is set to 0 ONCE, before the repeating part begins, and is not set to 0 again inside the repeating part.

rubric.title: One loop over numbers, closed
rubric.description: The steps go through the numbers as ONE repeating part (FOR EACH, loop through, repeat for each number, or similar) and say where the repeating part ends (END FOR, END LOOP, 'when there are no more numbers', or similar).

rubric.title: Each number is added to the total, inside the loop
rubric.description: Inside the repeating part, each number is added to the running total (total + number or similar), not just counted or replaced.

rubric.title: The total is given back after the loop
rubric.description: The finished total is returned, given back or shown once, after the repeating part has ended.

rubric.title: Nothing is given back inside the loop
rubric.description: No step inside the repeating part returns, gives back or shows the total. Giving it back happens only after the loop. If the student never wrote a loop at all, mark this missing.
